source_text: Καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐνενηκοστοῦ πέμπτου ψαλμοῦ τῶν διὰ Δαυῒδ λεχθέντων λόγων λέξεις βραχείας ἀφείλοντο ταύτας· ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου. Εἰρημένου γὰρ τοῦ λόγου· Εἴπατε ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν· Ὁ κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου, ἀφῆκαν· Εἴπατε ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν· Ὁ κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν . Ἐν δὲ τοῖς ἔθνεσι περὶ οὐδενὸς ὡς θεοῦ καὶ κυρίου ἐλέχθη ποτὲ ἀπὸ τῶν τοῦ γένους ὑμῶν ἀνθρώπων ὅτι ἐβασίλευσεν, ἀλλ᾿ ἢ περὶ τούτου μόνου τοῦ σταυρωθέντος. ὃν καὶ σεσῶσθαι ἀναστάντα ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ ψαλμῷ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἄγιον λέγει. μηνύον ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ὅμοιος τοῖς τῶν ἐθνῶν θεοῖς· ἐκεῖνα γὰρ εἴδωλά ἐστι δαιμονίων . Ἀλλ᾿ ὅπως τὸ λεγόμενον νοήσητε, τὸν πάντα ψαλμὸν ἀπαγγελῶ ὑμῖν. Ἔστι δὲ οὗτος· Ἄισατε τῷ κυρίῳ ᾆσμκ καινόν, ᾄσατε τῷ κυρίῳ πᾶσα ἡ γῆ. Ἄισατε τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ εὐλογῄσατε τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ· εὐαγγελίζεσθε ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας τὸ σωτήριον αὐτοῦ. Ἀναγγείλατε ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσι τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς λαοῖς τὰ θαυμάσια αὐτοῦ· ὅτι μέγας κύριος καὶ αἰνετὸς σφόδρα, φοβερός ἐστιν ὑπὲρ πάντας τοὺς θεούς· ὅτι πάντες οἱ θεοὶ τῶν ἐθνῶν δαιμόνια. ὁ δὲ κύριος τοὺς οὐρανοὺς ἐποίησεν. Ἐξομολόγησις καὶ ὡραιότης ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ. ἁγιωσύνη καὶ μεγαλοπρέπεια ἐν τῷ ἁγιάσματι αὐτοῦ. Ἐνέγκατε τῷ κυρίῳ, αἱ πατριαὶ τῶν ἐθνῶν, ἐνέγκατε τῷ κυρίῳ δόξαν καὶ τιμήν, ἐνέγκατε τῷ κυρίῳ δόξαν ἐν ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ. Αἴρετε θυσίας καὶ εἰσπορεύεσθε εἰς τὰς αὐλάς αὐτοῦ, προσκυνήσατε τῷ κυρίῳ ἐν αὐλῇ ἁγίᾳ αὐτοῦ. Σαλευθήτω ἀπὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ πᾶσα ἡ γῆ. Εἴπατε ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν· Ὁ κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου. Καὶ γὰρ κατώρθωσε τὴν οἰκουμένην. ἥτις οὐ σαλευθήσεται· κρινεῖ λαοὺς ἐν εὐθύτητι. Εὐφραινέσθωσαν οἱ οὐρανοί καὶ ἀγαλλιάσθω ἡ γῆ, σαλευθήσεται ἡ θάλασσα καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς. Χαρήσεται τὰ πεδία καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς, ἀγαλλιάσονται πάντα τὰ ξύλα τοῦ δρυμοῦ ἀπὸ προσώπου κυρίου. ὅτι ἔρχεται, ὅτι ἔρχεται κρῖναι τὴν γῆν. Κρινεῖ τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ λαοὺς ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ αὐτοῦ . Καὶ ὁ Τρύφων· Εἰ μέν. ὡς ἔφης. εἶπε, παρέγραψάν τι ἀπὸ τῶν γραφῶν οἱ ἄρχοντες τοῦ λαοῦ. θεὸς δύναται ἐπίστασθαι· ἀπίστῳ δὲ ἔοικε τὸ τοιοῦτον. Ναί. ἔφην, ἀπίστῳ ἔοικε· φοβερώτερον γάρ ἐστι τῆς μοσχοποιΐας, ἣν ἐποίησαν ἐπὶ γῆς μάννα πεπλησμένοι, καὶ τοῦ τὰ τέκνα θύειν τοῖς δαιμονίοις. ἢ τοῦ αὐτοὺς τοὺς προφήτας ἀνῃρηκέναι. Ἀλλὰ δή. ἔφην. μοι νομίζεσθε μηδὲ ἀκηκοέναι ἃς εἶπον περικεκοφέναι αὐτοὺς γραφάς. Ὑπὲρ αὐταρκείας γὰρ αἱ τοσαῦται προανιστορημέναι εἰσὶν εἰς ἀπόδειξιν τῶν ζητηθέντων μετὰ τῶν λεχθήσεσθαι μελλόντων παρ᾿ ὑμῖν παραπεφυλαγμένων.
pass_a_gloss: And from the ninety-fifth psalm of the words spoken through David, some brief phrases were removed, these: from the tree. For when the phrase was spoken: Say among the nations: The Lord reigns from the tree, they removed: Say among the nations: The Lord reigns. And among the nations, it was never spoken about any god and lord by people of your race that he reigns, except about this one who was crucified. Whom the Holy Spirit also says in the same psalm was resurrected. Indicating that he is not like the gods of the nations, for those are idols of demons. But so that you may understand what is being said, I will recite the entire psalm to you. It is as follows: Sing to the Lord a new song, sing to the Lord, all the earth. Sing to the Lord and bless his name, proclaim his salvation from day to day. Declare his glory among the nations, his wonders among all peoples. For the Lord is great and worthy of praise, he is feared above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are demons, but the Lord made the heavens. Confession and beauty are before him, holiness and majesty in his sanctuary. Bring to the Lord, O families of the nations, bring to the Lord glory and honor, bring to the Lord glory in his name. Take up sacrifices and come into his courts, worship the Lord in his holy court. Let all the earth tremble before him. Say among the nations: The Lord reigns from the tree. For he has brought about the salvation of the world, which will not be shaken. He will judge the peoples with uprightness. Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad, let the sea and its fullness be shaken. Let the fields be joyful and all that is in them, let all the trees of the forest sing before the Lord. For he is coming, for he is coming to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with his truth. And Trypho said: If, as you said, the rulers of the people have written something down from the scriptures, God is able to know, but it seems unbelievable. Yes, I said, it seems unbelievable, for it is more frightening than the idol-making, which they did on earth when they were full of manna, and the sacrificing of children to demons, or the killing of the prophets themselves. But come now, I said, do you think you have not even heard what I said about the scriptures being cut off? For the many prophecies that have been spoken beforehand are sufficient for the proof of the things being sought, along with the things that will be said and are being reserved for you.

pass_b_english: From the ninety-fifth psalm, the words spoken through David, some brief phrases were removed — specifically, the words 'from the tree.' For when the line was spoken: 'Say among the nations: The Lord reigns from the tree,' they struck out 'from the tree' and left only: 'Say among the nations: The Lord reigns' (Psalm 96:10). Yet among the nations, it was never said of any god or lord by people of your race that he reigns — except of this one who was crucified. The Holy Spirit also says in the same psalm that he would be saved by rising again, indicating that he is not like the gods of the nations, for those are idols of demons (Psalm 96:5).

But so that you may understand what is being said, I will recite the entire psalm to you. It runs: Sing to the Lord a new song; sing to the Lord, all the earth. Sing to the Lord and bless his name; proclaim his salvation from day to day. Declare his glory among the nations, his wonders among all peoples. For the Lord is great and worthy of all praise; he is feared above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are demons, but the Lord made the heavens. Confession and beauty stand before him; holiness and majesty fill his sanctuary. Bring to the Lord, you families of the nations, bring to the Lord glory and honor; bring to the Lord glory in his name. Take up sacrifices and enter his courts; worship the Lord in his holy court. Let all the earth tremble before him. Say among the nations: 'The Lord reigns from the tree' (Psalm 96:1–10).

For he has established the world so that it will not be shaken; he will judge the peoples with uprightness. Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad; let the sea and its fullness roar. Let the fields exult and everything in them; let all the trees of the forest sing for joy before the Lord. For he is coming, for he is coming to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with his truth (Psalm 96:10–13).

Then Trypho said: 'If, as you say, the rulers of the people have removed something from the Scriptures, God is able to know — but such a thing seems unbelievable.' I answered: 'Yes, it seems unbelievable — yet it is more frightening than the making of the golden calf, which they did on earth while gorged on manna, or the sacrificing of children to demons, or the killing of the prophets themselves. But come now — do you suppose you have not even heard what I said about the Scriptures being cut off? For the many prophecies spoken beforehand are sufficient proof of the matters under investigation, together with the things still to be said, which are being reserved for you.'
